chapters.prompt: What happened to the model engine Peter got for his birthday?
choices: It was lost on a train
It went off with a bang and broke
Phyllis gave it away
It was stolen from the nursery
chapters.evidence: Then, owing either to Peter's inexperience or Phyllis's good intentions... the Engine suddenly went off with a bang.

chapters.prompt: What happened on the evening Father was looking at the broken engine?
choices: The house caught fire
Aunt Emma arrived to stay
A letter came from the King
Two gentlemen came, and Father was called away
chapters.evidence: two gentlemen wanted to see the master ... “Father's been called away—on business,” said Mother.

chapters.prompt: What did Mother ask the children not to do?
choices: Ask any questions about the trouble
Play in the garden
Go outside after dark
Write letters to Father
chapters.evidence: “I want you not to ask me any questions about this trouble; and not to ask anybody else any questions.”

chapters.prompt: Where was the supper Mrs. Viney had left for the family?
choices: In the cellar with the packing cases
At Mrs. Viney's own house
In a small room they thought was a cupboard
On the kitchen table under a cloth
chapters.evidence: The forgotten room opened out of the kitchen... its door had been mistaken for a cupboard's.

chapters.prompt: Why did Peter start taking coal?
choices: He wanted to sell it in the village
Mother said they were too poor to have a fire
The Station Master asked him to
He needed it for his model engine
chapters.evidence: “You know that wet day? Well, Mother said we were too poor to have a fire.”

chapters.prompt: What did the Station Master decide to do after catching Peter?
choices: Take him to the police station
Tell Mother everything
Make him work at the station
Let him off this once, with a warning
chapters.evidence: “I'll look over it this once. But you remember, young gentleman, stealing is stealing”

chapters.prompt: How did the children first get to know the old gentleman?
choices: He waved back when they waved at his train
He was an old friend of Father's
He came to Three Chimneys for tea
He worked as the station porter
chapters.evidence: And out of a first-class carriage a hand waved back... It was the old gentleman's hand.

chapters.prompt: When Mother was ill, how did the children get the old gentleman's attention?
choices: They shouted at his train from the bridge
They sent a telegram to London
They painted big letters on a white sheet by the line
They asked the Doctor to visit him
chapters.evidence: a large white sheet nailed against the fence. On the sheet there were thick black letters more than a foot long.

chapters.prompt: What did the old gentleman send to the children?
choices: A letter saying he could not help
A hamper with the things Mother needed, and more
Money to pay the doctor
A new model engine for Peter
chapters.evidence: Then the children undid the hamper... then came all the things they had asked for, and plenty of them

chapters.prompt: After hearing about the hamper, what did Mother make the children promise?
choices: Never to go to the station again
Never to wave at trains again
To pay the old gentleman back
Never to ask strangers to give them things
chapters.evidence: “And you must never, never, never ask strangers to give you things.”

chapters.prompt: What did Bobbie ask the Doctor on her birthday?
choices: If he would mend Peter's engine
If her family could join his Club, like Mrs. Viney
If he knew where Father was
If he would come to her birthday tea
chapters.evidence: “Can't we be in the Club, too, the same as Mrs. Viney?”

chapters.prompt: Why did Bobbie climb up into the engine's cab?
choices: To get a free ride to London
To hide from the Station Master
To ask the men to mend Peter's toy engine
To look for Peter and Phyllis
chapters.evidence: “I only wanted to ask you if you'd be so kind as to mend this.”

chapters.prompt: How did the children find out which country the stranger came from?
choices: He wrote its name on paper
He picked a Russian stamp from Peter's stamps
The Station Master read his ticket
He drew them a map
chapters.evidence: The hand that he reached out at last... contained a RUSSIAN stamp.

chapters.prompt: Why had the Russian been sent to prison in his own country?
choices: He had stolen a horse
He had started a fire
He had broken into a bank
He had written a book about helping poor people
chapters.evidence: he wrote a beautiful book about poor people and how to help them... And they sent him to prison for it.

chapters.prompt: Who was the Russian hoping to find in England?
choices: His wife and children
An old school friend
A doctor for his cough
The man who printed his book
chapters.evidence: his wife and children had escaped and come to England. So when he deserted he came here to look for them.

chapters.prompt: Why was Perks cross with the children at first?
choices: They had broken one of his lamps
They had walked on the line
Nobody had told him the Russian's story
They picked his strawberries without asking
chapters.evidence: “Not so much as a breath... But I did think one o' you would 'a' nipped down to tell me”

chapters.prompt: What did the children see happen at the railway cutting?
choices: A train came off the rails
Rocks, earth and trees slid down onto the line
A fire started in the trees
A bridge fell into the canal
chapters.evidence: rock and trees and grass and bushes... slipped right away from the face of the cutting and fell on the line

chapters.prompt: What did the children use to make red warning flags?
choices: Peter's red scarf
A red tablecloth from home
Handkerchiefs dipped in paint
The girls' red flannel petticoats
chapters.evidence: “How lucky we DID put on our red flannel petticoats!” said Phyllis.

chapters.prompt: What did the railway give each child at the presentation?
choices: A medal on a ribbon
A model steam-engine
A gold watch and chain
A free ticket to London
chapters.evidence: he called the children one by one, by their names, and gave each of them a beautiful gold watch and chain.

chapters.prompt: What did Bobbie ask the old gentleman to help with?
choices: Finding the Russian's wife and children
Getting Peter a job on the railway
Paying the doctor's bill
Sending a letter to Father
chapters.evidence: “And what we want more than anything in the world is to find his wife and children for him,” said Bobbie

chapters.prompt: About ten days later, what news did the old gentleman bring to Three Chimneys?
choices: He was moving to the village
The Russian had to leave England
The railway was building a new station
He had found the Russian's wife and child
chapters.evidence: “Good news,” said he. “I've found your Russian friend's wife and child”

chapters.prompt: Why did the bargeman grab Peter by the ear?
choices: Peter threw coal at his barge
He thought the children were fishing in his waters
Peter untied his barge
Peter had frightened his horse
chapters.evidence: “Don't you know these 'ere waters is preserved? You ain't no right catching fish 'ere”

chapters.prompt: Who carried the baby out of the smoky barge cabin?
choices: Bobbie
Phyllis
Peter
Bill the bargeman
chapters.evidence: picked it up and backed out... “I've got the kid,” said Peter, tearing off the handkerchief and staggering on to the deck.

chapters.prompt: How did Bill the bargeman thank the children?
choices: He gave them each a shilling
He gave them a puppy
He wrote a letter to their Mother
He took them on a free barge trip
chapters.evidence: “I'll take you the entire trip to Farley and back, so I will, and not a penny to pay.”

chapters.prompt: How did the children collect presents for Perks's birthday?
choices: They asked people in the village to give things
They spent Mother's story money
They made everything themselves
The Station Master bought them
chapters.evidence: “There must be lots of people in the village who'd like to help to make him a birthday. Let's go round and ask everybody.”

chapters.prompt: Why was Perks angry when he first saw all the presents?
choices: He did not like buns
Some of the presents were broken
He thought they were charity
He wanted money instead
chapters.evidence: “I'm not going to begin these sort of charity goings-on at my time of life”

chapters.prompt: What changed Perks's mind about the presents?
choices: The Station Master ordered him to keep them
Bobbie read out what each giver had said about him
The old gentleman came to visit
The Doctor explained it to him
chapters.evidence: “we wrote down all the things everybody said when they gave us the things, with the people's names”

chapters.prompt: How did Peter hurt his foot?
choices: He fell over and the rake's teeth cut it
He stepped on a nail in the stable
He dropped the coal-shovel on it
He tripped on the railway line
chapters.evidence: there were three red wounds in Peter's foot and ankle, where the teeth of the rake had bitten him

chapters.prompt: Why had Bobbie stopped talking about Father to Mother?
choices: She was cross with Father
She thought it made Mother more unhappy
Peter told her not to
She had forgotten about him
chapters.evidence: “I thought you were so unhappy about Daddy not being here, it made you worse when I talked about him.”

chapters.prompt: What did Bobbie read on the old newspaper wrapped around the magazines?
choices: Father had won a prize
The railway was closing
Father had been found guilty at a trial
The Russian was going home
chapters.evidence: The name of the man who had been tried was the name of her Father. The verdict was 'Guilty.'

chapters.prompt: What was Father wrongly accused of?
choices: Stealing coal from the railway
Selling State secrets, like a spy
Robbing a bank
Setting fire to his office
chapters.evidence: charging him with selling State secrets to the Russians—with being, in fact, a spy and a traitor.

chapters.prompt: What did Bobbie do to try to help Father?
choices: Wrote to the old gentleman and sent him the newspaper report
Told Peter and Phyllis the secret
Went to London on the train
Wrote a letter to the newspaper
chapters.evidence: once more she wrote a letter. And once more it was to the old gentleman.

chapters.prompt: Why did the children go into the tunnel?
choices: To take a shortcut home
To hide from a train
The runner in the red jersey never came out
To look for Phyllis's lost bootlace
chapters.evidence: But though they waited and waited and waited, the boy in the red jersey did not appear.

chapters.prompt: What was wrong with Jim, the boy in the red jersey?
choices: He had broken his leg
He had lost his way
He had hurt his arm in a fight
He had been hit by the train
chapters.evidence: “Bother! I believe I've broken my leg,” he said.

chapters.prompt: What did Peter and Phyllis find in the signal-box?
choices: It was empty and locked
Perks was on duty there
The Doctor was inside
The signalman was fast asleep
chapters.evidence: The signalman was sitting on a chair tilted back against the wall... He was fast asleep.

chapters.prompt: Where did the children decide to take Jim?
choices: To their own home, Three Chimneys
To his school in Maidbridge
To Brigden's farm
To the station
chapters.evidence: “Then we're to take him up to Three Chimneys?” said the bailiff. “Of course,” said Peter.

chapters.prompt: Why did Bobbie and Phyllis tie Peter up?
choices: He kept talking about blood and wounds after they asked him to stop
He had broken Phyllis's doll
They were playing prisoners
To stop him waking Jim
chapters.evidence: “It was only that I kept on talking about blood and wounds... And I wouldn't stop when they asked me.”

chapters.prompt: Who turned out to be Jim's grandfather?
choices: Dr. Forrest
The Station Master
The old gentleman
Bill the bargeman
chapters.evidence: “Jim's grandfather has come,” ... “It's our own old gentleman!” said Phyllis.

chapters.prompt: What did the old gentleman tell Bobbie privately at the gate?
choices: He was taking Jim away the next day
Mother must go back to her writing
He wanted them all to visit London
He was certain Father was innocent, and had hopes
chapters.evidence: “But I have hopes, my dear—I have hopes.” ... “I'm perfectly CERTAIN he didn't.”

chapters.prompt: What was unusual when the children waved to the 9.15 train?
choices: The train did not come
People waved from every window
The old gentleman did not wave
The train stopped by the fence
chapters.evidence: from every window handkerchiefs fluttered, newspapers signalled, hands waved wildly.

chapters.prompt: Who did Bobbie meet getting off the 11.54 train?
choices: The Russian gentleman
Jim's schoolmaster
Aunt Emma
Father
chapters.evidence: “Oh! my Daddy, my Daddy!” That scream went like a knife into the heart of everyone in the train

chapters.prompt: Why was Father able to come home?
choices: He had escaped
He had paid a fine
The man who really did it had been caught
The Russian had spoken up for him
chapters.evidence: “They've caught the man who did it. Everyone knows now that it wasn't your Daddy.”
